summary: Preinstall DNS exfiltration of installer hostname and username via OAST collector
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node poc.js', which fires automatically on npm install. poc.js reads os.hostname() and os.userInfo().username, encodes them as `${username}.${hostname}.<subdomain>.oast.fun`, and issues a dns.lookup() against that name, causing the installer's host and user identifiers to leak to the oast.fun out-of-band interaction collector via authoritative DNS. The package's own metadata self-describes as a 'Dependency Confusion PoC' at version 99.9.9 — a version-inflation pattern intended to win npm resolution against an internally named package 'reactjs-risk', so that any organization with an internal package of that name accidentally pulls this public artifact and triggers the exfiltration on install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
